sentences.text: CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY DHAR, JUDGE (JUDGMENT) Heard and considered.
The instant application, in view of the reasons stated therein, coupled with the submissions made at bar, is allowed.
The delay in filing the review petition is condoned and the review petition is taken on board.

CM disposed of.
1.

Through the medium of the instant review petition, the petitioner is seeking review of the judgment passed by this Court on 06.06.2023, whereby the appeal filed by the review petitioner against judgment dated 05.11.2015, passed by Principal District Judge, Pulwama, has been partly allowed and the impugned judgment passed by the learned trial court has been modified to the extent that the land owners have been held entitled to compensation @ Rs.3.00 lacs per kanal instead of Rs.5.00 lacs, as was awarded by the trial court.

It has been further provided that the land owners shall be entitled to Jabirana @ 15% and interest @ 6% on the enhanced amount from the date of issuance of notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act till the actual payment of the enhanced compensation.

Heard and considered.

3. It has been contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that while passing the judgment under review, this Court has observed that the Revenue Minister in terms of the provisions contained in sub-section (3) of Section 11 of the J&K Land Acquisition Act, approved the rate of Rs. 3.00 lacs per kanal but as per the record, the Revenue Minister accepted the rate of Rs. 2.00 lacs per kanal, as recommended by the Tehsildar.

In this regard, the learned counsel has placed reliance upon communication No.11-Rev(LAK)94-Pulwama, dated 14.12.1999, addressed by Additional Secretary to Government, Revenue Department, whereby Collector, Land Acquisition, Pulwama, has been conveyed approval of the Revenue Minister to the adoption of rates of compensation @ Rs.2.00 lacs per kanal.
The learned counsel has submitted that the extracts of the aforesaid letter also find mention in the award dated 30.03.2000, passed by the Collector.

On this ground, it is urged that the impugned judgment has been passed without taking note of the aforesaid documents and, as such, it constitutes an error apparent on the face of record entailing review of the impugned judgment.

4. A perusal of the record of reference would reveal that the Collector, after passing the tentative award, referred the matter to the Revenue Minister in terms of the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of Section 11 of the J&K Land Acquisition Act for approval.

The note sheets contained in the record of the Collector reveal that the Revenue Minister, vide his detailed note dated 12.01.1999, has observed that the Collector has not taken into consideration all the issues at the time of fixation of rates and according to the Revenue Minister, the compensation to the extent of Rs.3.00 lacs per kanal is justifiable in the instant case.
5. Again, in note dated 18.10.1999, recorded by the Revenue Minister, it has been clearly stated that the rate of Rs. 3.00 lacs per kanal would be in consonance with the just provisions of law.

It would be apt to reproduce the relevant excerpts of note dated 18.10.1999:
"

(109) It is relevant to state here that on the request of the land owners, I have held an enquiry in the matter and also called for a report from concerned subordinate authorities regarding the prevailing market value of the land in the vicinity of land under acquisition.
I have also visited the spot and have gone through the tentative award statement as submitted by the Collector, Land Acq. Pulwama.
He has in detail stated that potentialities of the land in question both for commercial as well as construction purposes.
The land in question in fact, is hardly 20 to 30 feet away from Srinagar National Highway.
The HPC Ltd, the intending party, has started operations for setting up the Bottling Plant which is nearing completion.
A petrol Pump has been set up on the land which is in operation and the earnings have started.
The said Corpn. is a multimillionaire concern and should not ordinarily thrive at the cost of poor land owners without paying them reasonable and fair compensation.
Further, the land which is their main source of income and certainly has very good potentialities of future use as well for commercial and Industrial purposes.

Hindustan Petroleum vs Bashandgan Namblabal on 10 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88347696/
2

(110)The Intending party i.e., HPC Ltd; has not to wait any more for starting its business operations and appears to have very bright chances to earn Lakhs of rupees in the business they are going to start by setting up a Bottling Plant and Petrol Pump etc.
They must as such pay fair and genuine and reasonable compensation to the land-Owners.
Such cases have been also discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in various of its judgements especially in a judgement reported in AIR, 1988.

(111) In view of what has been stated in detail herein above, I determine the proper value of the land under acquisition under the provisions of Section 11, Sub Section-3 at Rupees 3 Lakhs per kanal to which the land owners are entitled to in consonance with the just provisions of law relating to the determination of value of property to be acquired compulsorily for a public purpose from the land owners whose main source of livelihood is the land to be taken from them.

(112) This will be communicated to the Collector, Land- Acq. Pulwama and the file along with all relevant papers returned to him who shall make an award as required under Sub Sec.4 of Sec.11 of the Land Acq. Act without taking much time as the land owners have been kept waiting for so many years for finalization of the award of compensation and payment thereof to them.

6. From a perusal of the afore-quoted note of the Revenue Minister, it is clear that the said authority has undertaken enquiry after the matter was submitted to him by the Collector in terms of sub-section (2) of Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act.
Thereafter the Revenue Minister has determined the value of the land under acquisition as Rs.3.00 lacs per kanal.

While doing so, the Revenue Minister has exercised his powers under sub-section (3) of Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act and the matter has been referred back to the Collector for making an award.

The only option available with the Collector in these circumstances was to make an award in terms of the directions of the Revenue Minister and any award made in contravention of these directions as per the provisions contained in sub-section (5) of Section 11 of the Act would be void.
7.
It seems that it is on this basis that the award came to be formulated by the Collector.

8. Once the matter was referred by the Collector to the Revenue Minister in terms of sub-section (2)
of Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act and the Revenue Minister undertook an enquiry and recorded a finding that the land owners deserve to be granted compensation @ Rs.3.00 lacs per kanal and at the same time directed the Collector to pass an award accordingly, there was no occasion for the subordinate authorities to again refer the matter to the Revenue Minister.

There is no provision in the Land Acquisition Act which provides for review of the decision made by the Revenue Minister in exercise of his power under sub-section (3) of Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Even otherwise, while reviewing his decision, the Revenue Minister has stuck to the stand that the market rate of the acquired land earlier assessed by him appears to be genuine but somehow, he has agreed with the recommendation of the Tehsildar without assigning any reason.

3 9.
For the foregoing reasons, even after taking into consideration the subsequent noting recorded by the Revenue Minister, the course of the judgment under review would not get altered.

The petition,
therefore, is without any merit and is dismissed accordingly.
10. The record be sent back.
(Sanjay Dhar) Judge Srinagar 10.08.2023
"Bhat Altaf, PS"
